title: Deterministic almost-linear vertex connectivity
formal: Is there a uniform deterministic algorithm computing the exact vertex connectivity and a minimum vertex separator of every simple unweighted undirected graph in \((m+n)^{1+o(1)}\) worst-case time on a word RAM?
definitions: The input is a finite simple undirected graph with labelled vertex set \([n]\), \(n\ge2\), and an explicit list of \(m\) edges; isolated vertices are included. For \(S\subseteq V\), delete its vertices and incident edges. The vertex connectivity \(\kappa(G)\) is the minimum \(|S|\) for which the remaining graph is disconnected or has at most one vertex. For a disconnected input it is zero, and \(\kappa(K_{n})=n-1\). Output both \(\kappa(G)\) and an attaining set \(S\). Use a uniform word RAM with word length \(w=d\lceil\log_{2}(n+2)\rceil\), for a fixed positive integer \(d\) chosen with the algorithm and large enough for its addresses and input values. Unit-cost instructions are word reads/writes, copying, comparisons, branching, Boolean operations, shifts, addition, subtraction and multiplication modulo \(2^{w}\), and integer quotient and remainder with nonzero divisor. Shifts by at least \(w\) return zero. Multiword computation is charged by its component instructions. The fixed finite program receives no advice or precomputed tables; all initialization, preprocessing and output writes count. Write \(N=m+n\). Almost-linear time means that there exist one algorithm, a constant \(C\) and a function \(h:\mathbb{N}\to[1,\infty)\), independent of the input graph, with \(\lim_{N\to\infty}\log h(N)/\log N=0\), such that the time is at most \(CNh(N)\) for every input. All hidden constants are independent of the graph. No randomness is allowed, and the bound must hold for all connectivity values, including those growing with the graph size.

context_blocks.text: Vertex connectivity measures how many vertex failures a network can withstand. Its global nature requires the weakest separation to be found without specifying the separated vertices.

Li, Nanongkai, Panigrahi, Saranurak and Yingchareonthawornchai give a randomized reduction to a polylogarithmic number of maximum-flow computations. Together with modern exact flow algorithms this yields randomized almost-linear time.

The 2025 deterministic bound is \(m\kappa\,n^{o(1)}\), with \(\kappa\) the connectivity. It resolves important smaller-connectivity regimes but retains a polynomial overhead when connectivity is large.
Both lines build on the earlier vertex-connectivity algorithms of Henzinger, Rao and Gabow. The remaining demand is a uniform deterministic bound over all graphs.

why: Closing the deterministic gap for a basic network robustness measure would establish the computational role of randomness in a major exact graph primitive.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated existence claim or its logical negation, with the specified model, quantifiers and guarantees. A conditional lower bound settles only its conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean; a partial improvement does not meet the target.

sentences: Vertex connectivity is the smallest number of vertices whose removal disconnects a graph or leaves at most one vertex.
The task is to find this number and an attaining separator in an unweighted undirected graph.
The question asks for deterministic almost-linear worst-case time.
Randomized almost-linear algorithms are known, while the reviewed deterministic bound still depends on the connectivity.
The target tests the role of randomness in exact network robustness computation.
